articles.title: The hidden costs of fracking: boom in Argentina linked to trail of sickness
articles.summary:
Families in Vaca Muerta, the centre of Patagonia’s shale operation, report cancers, miscarriages and pollution

In Allen, a small town in Argentine Patagonia, many people living on the same street ended up falling ill. For some, it was severe migraines, nausea or skin irritation. For others, cancers, congenital abnormalities, miscarriages or stillbirth seemed to affect foetuses or children. People say it all started 13 years ago – when a well was drilled near their homes to extract gas and oil.

Calle Ciega 10 [Dead-end Street 10] lies on the eastern edge of Vaca Muerta, a vital area for Argentina’s economy, home to the world’s second-largest reserve of shale gas and fourth-largest reserve of shale oil. The region has more than 2,600 active wells, including one on this small street where about 20 families live, most of them seasonal workers on fruit farms.

articles.title: Mistura review – ice queen brings Peruvian culinary drama to a gentle simmer
articles.summary:
Bárbara Mori stars in tepid tale of a high-society wife who opens a restaurant in her home after her husband leaves her

What you expect from a film about a fancy high-end restaurant is a certain amount of heat: the roiling intensity of staff pushed to their absolute limits in the pursuit of gastronomic perfection. But this 1960s-set Peruvian drama instead maintains a gentle simmer, sedate and elegant. Perhaps it’s too elegant given the circumstances of its chef-proprietor, a high-society trophy wife with no catering experience who makes a high-stakes gamble on opening a successful restaurant.

Bárbara Mori is Norma, a glacial beauty who cultivates a kind of Jackie Onassis chic: huge sunglasses, massive blow-dry, makeup thickly applied like armour. One night, Norma’s husband humiliatingly leaves her for a beauty queen. You’d be sympathetic if Norma wasn’t so foul to the staff, lashing out at housekeeper Rosa (Hermelinda Luján) and chauffeur Oscar (Cesar Ballumbrosio). It’s Oscar (who is a bit in love with Norma) who suggests she opens a restaurant in the house to pay the mortgage. Norma’s father was the French ambassador to Peru, and she has picked up his passion for gastronomy. Although the script is a bit inconsistent on this, since Oscar also says he’s never seen her so much as light the oven.

It means that Mitchell can now vote in US elections, something that she had complained she wasn’t able to do.

International pressure remains concentrated on Venezuela following new torture charges against Nicolas Maduro and the arrest of key figures linked to corruption.

Regional economic sentiment is dampened by the IMF's downward growth revisions and disruptions from the El Niño weather pattern affecting infrastructure and tourism in Argentina. Meanwhile, expanding international operations of organized crime and cocaine trafficking continue to exert severe pressure on security forces across the continent.
archive.forecast_cs: V příštích dnech lze očekávat další vyostřování brazilské předvolební kampaně a zvýšenou ostražitost investorů vůči latinskoamerickým aktivům v důsledku zhoršených makroekonomických prognóz MMF.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, further escalation of the Brazilian election campaign is expected, alongside heightened investor caution toward Latin American assets following the IMF's downgraded macroeconomic forecasts.

archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, further diplomatic clashes between Argentina and the UK over Falklands oil projects and hardening rhetoric in Brazil's presidential campaign are expected.
